newsitem.title: USA: Boeing denies U.S. helicopter allegations.
newsitem.headline: Boeing denies U.S. helicopter allegations.

text.p: Boeing Co Thursday denied a federal charges that it knowingly used defective parts obtained from a subcontractor in U.S. Army CH-47D Chinook helicopters.
"The company believes that the government's decision to pursue this matter is uninformed and unjustified," Boeing said in a written statement.
The Justice Department Thursday said it has joined a "whistleblower" lawsuit filed against the aerospace giant by a former employee of a Boeing subcontractor.
Boeing said the plaintiff in the case, filed under the federal False Claims Act, was a "disgruntled" former employee of Speco Corp., which is out of business and not a party to the lawsuit.
The lawsuit charges that the faulty gears caused the crashes of two helicopters in 1991 and 1993, resulting in damage to the aircaraft but no loss of life.
Boeing said it spent $2 million inspecting the Chinook fleet after the accidents and relaced about 35 gears.
"Both of the gears that failed were manufactured by Speco prior to 1990," Boeing said in its statement. The company said no gears had failed since Speco changed its manufacturing processes in 1991.
Since then the fleet has logged more than 300,000 flight hours "without a single gear failure," Boeing said.
"The government's allegations of civil false claims by Boeing are not supported by any evidence and are based on uninformed suspicions and conjecture," the company said.
